# StructuPath Herdr Suite

> Herdr-native tools for human-supervised agent work. Explore is the ready first workflow; Deliver is an advanced assembly pattern; Browser and Guard are supporting capabilities.

Landing and first Explore run: https://herdr.structupath.ai/
Canonical docs: https://herdr.structupath.ai/docs/
Source Markdown: https://github.com/StructuPath/herdr-suite-site/tree/main/docs-src
Pinned evidence: https://github.com/StructuPath/herdr-suite-site/blob/main/data/plugins.json

## Workflow taxonomy

### Explore — ready first workflow

Swarm (`structupath.swarm`) release 0.3.0: Herdr >=0.7.4; historical evidence records 0.7.4 and 0.7.5 paths. It gives one bounded task to parallel worktree agents, reports candidate changes, and provides review-first harvest. Agents commit locally; the operator can explicitly publish a slot branch with an ordinary push for PR review. Publication does not create a PR. The operator defines comparison criteria, reviews diffs/tests, and selects what lands.

A clean-slot selection in Harvest performs a `--no-ff` merge. When the base is not checked out, a plugin-owned merge worktree can advance the base ref after preview without another confirmation screen. Treat selection as approval. Abort preserves branches. Removing ignored files requires exact one-use inventory-bound cleanup approval, not a generic yes.

Guide: https://herdr.structupath.ai/docs/swarm/

### Deliver — attended Stage 3

Conductor (`structupath.conductor`) release 0.4.0: requires exactly Herdr 0.7.5, protocol 17, API schema 1. Historical Stage 2 evidence is retained. A separate 2026-09-14 developer smoke exercised all seven installed actions on Herdr 0.7.5, including preview, attended apply, replay, and completed stand-down after fixing its omitted reason. It used synthetic local workers and operator-produced reports; it is not real-agent certification or formal release attestation. Its seven actions are assemble, board, status, harvest, preview, apply, and stand-down. It runs task-bound roles with strict state, deterministic integration, exact-SHA gates, and attended preview/apply to one local ref. Config version 3 requires apply:null to disable publication or an explicit target_ref to enable it; version 2 remains supported with apply disabled.

An operator drives each transition, reviews preview, and supplies a canonical approval receipt using the exact returned command. Worker approval reports are not operator receipts. Apply durably consumes the receipt once before zero or one local-ref compare-and-swap. Only apply can resolve its uncertain publication using exact target observations; general ambiguous recovery remains refused. There is no remote push, deployment, authenticated approval, suite adapter, unattended automation, cryptographic report attestation, or same-user security boundary.

Guide: https://herdr.structupath.ai/docs/conductor/

## Supporting trust capabilities

- Browser (`structupath.browser`) release 0.7.0: Herdr >=0.7.0; evidence records testing with 0.7.4. Launch local Chromium, attach to an existing CDP browser, or share an agent-browser session. Node 22+ is required for launch, attach, and streaming; Node 20 supports shared-session polling. Recording observation bundles require agent-browser and are not test acceptance. Observe-only configuration blocks pane input and link navigation; the runtime toggle alone does not block launcher navigation in agent-browser mode. Sessions and persistent profiles are a trusted same-user boundary; recordings may be sensitive. https://herdr.structupath.ai/docs/browser/
- Guard (`structupath.guard`) release 0.2.0: minimum Herdr 0.7.5; historical pane integration evidence records 0.7.5. Advisory rendered-text audit, alerts, and interrupt attempts cannot prove prevention. Optional explicitly wired Claude PreToolUse Bash reporter evaluates commands before execution, but fails open on missing, timed-out, or invalid socket responses. Existing rules survive upgrades; Reset rules explicitly backs up and reseeds defaults. Neither path is a sandbox. https://herdr.structupath.ai/docs/guard/

## Trust and composition boundaries

- The four plugins do not form one automatic runtime pipeline.
- Swarm independently creates and harvests Swarm-owned worktrees for interchangeable fan-out agents.
- Conductor creates and reconciles Conductor-owned worktrees itself; it does not delegate worktree creation or harvest to Swarm.
- Write-capable agents and plugins are trusted same-user principals. Worktrees isolate changes for review, not filesystem or process access.
- Guard's pane watcher sees rendered terminal text; its optional reporter receives harness Bash commands. Native harness, sandbox, and operating-system controls remain authoritative.

## Install by capability

`herdr plugin install StructuPath/herdr-swarm`
`herdr plugin install StructuPath/herdr-conductor`
`herdr plugin install StructuPath/herdr-browser`
`herdr plugin install StructuPath/herdr-guard`

These commands are not a blanket marketplace-availability claim. Inspect each manifest and repository before installing same-user plugin code.
